key_insight: OpenGEM26 expands molecular machine-learning force-field training with 4.4 million DFT conformations from 200,000 organic molecules, enabling GPTFF-mol to model energies and forces more accurately across broader chemical and conformational space.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate for DFT in atomistic simulation of sulfur- and chlorine-containing organics, reducing computational cost while preserving reliable geometry, dynamics, and barrier predictions.
method: Built OpenGEM26 from optimization trajectories and non-equilibrium structures for H/C/N/O/S/Cl molecules with up to ten heavy atoms.
Computed labels at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP with dispersion corrections.
Trained a graph neural network potential, GPTFF-mol, on the resulting large-scale dataset.
evidence_signal: The paper reports GPTFF-mol reaches 16 meV/molecule (0.82 meV/atom) energy MAE and outperforms ANI-2x on force prediction, while reproducing butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization behavior.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on molecules with up to ten heavy atoms, so generalization to larger chemistries or very different reaction classes may require additional validation.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
